basics.name: Digital joinery catalogues and open systems: 50 Digital Wood Joints (Jochen Gros and Friedrich Sulzer, C-Lab, HfG Offenbach), WikiHouse Skylark (Open Systems Lab) and IBOIS EPFL timber joinery tools (Manis plate joinery solver, compas_wood, Robeller's integral plate joints)
basics.url: No single home page. 50 Digital Wood Joints: https://winterdienst.info/50-digital-wood-joints-by-jochen-gros/ (download https://jochen-gros.de/A/C-Lab_files/Digital_Wood_Joints_Complete.zip, poster https://jochen-gros.de/A/C-Lab_files/50%20digital%20joints.pdf, project page https://jochen-gros.de/A/C-Lab.html, mirror https://openup.design/we-learn/50-digital-wood-joints/). WikiHouse: https://www.wikihouse.cc/blocks and https://www.wikihouse.cc/engineering/bow-ties (repo https://github.com/wikihouseproject/Skylark). IBOIS: https://www.epfl.ch/labs/ibois/index-html/tools/ (Manis https://github.com/ibois-epfl/Manis-timber-plate-joinery-solver, compas_wood docs https://petrasvestartas.github.io/compas_wood/latest/)
basics.resource_type: classification system + CAD library (Gros's 50 joints with CAD/CAM files and PDF guide) + open building system (WikiHouse block library) + interactive tools / GitHub repos (IBOIS Grasshopper and Python joinery generators)
basics.cost: Free. Gros joints: free 49 to 51 MB download and free poster PDF. WikiHouse: free block files; paid optional design-check and manufacturing services. IBOIS tools: free and open source, but they run inside Rhino + Grasshopper (paid, about USD 1,000 for a Rhino licence [uncertain]); Manis's structural analysis also needs a paid Abaqus licence
basics.license: Gros joints: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 on winterdienst.info; Open Up! lists CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the re-organised cutting files on GitHub (ayseesindurmaz) say CC BY-SA 4.0 but credit Gros and Sulzer and reserve commercial credit to them. So: free to share and adapt with credit, non-commercial, share-alike. WikiHouse Skylark: CC BY-SA 4.0 (commercial use allowed, improvements must be re-shared; the name 'WikiHouse' is a trademark). Manis: MIT (Copyright 2021 IBOIS, EPFL). compas_wood: MIT (Petras Vestartas)
basics.language: 50 Digital Wood Joints: English and German (the CD package has parallel ENGLISH and DEUTSCH folders; the C-Lab project page is in German). WikiHouse and IBOIS tools: English
basics.year: Gros joints: C-Lab founded 1993, published as a CD-ROM in 1997; zip file last modified September 2016; winterdienst page April/May 2018; poster laid out by Meredith Scheff-King (Make: article December 2014); Open Up! mirror October 2023. WikiHouse: started summer 2011 (Alastair Parvin and Nick Ierodiaconou of 00); Skylark system about 2020, Skylark v1.0 repo release current in 2026. IBOIS: Robeller's integral joints PhD 2011 to 2015; Manis 2021 (Automation in Construction vol. 130); compas_wood docs updated in 2026 (unreleased changelog entries)
basics.access_barrier: none for the Gros download and WikiHouse files; desktop install for IBOIS tools (Rhino 7/8 with Grasshopper on Windows, plus Robots plugin, COMPAS and Abaqus for the full Manis workflow); the Gros CAD files are in 1990s formats (DGN, IGES, DXF R10 and CAM formats) that need a CAD program to open
basics.image_license: Gros drawings and PDF guide: same CC BY-NC-SA as the joints. WikiHouse images and guides: CC BY-SA ('most WikiHouse files and information'). IBOIS: MIT code; figures in papers are publisher copyright (Elsevier, ASCE) [uncertain]
basics.authority_level: Gros: educator (design school research lab, HfG Offenbach). WikiHouse: community/open-source with engineering testing (University of Strathclyde bow-tie tests; peer-reviewed Materials 2025 paper on TIE joints). IBOIS: academic peer-reviewed (EPFL timber construction lab, Prof. Yves Weinand)

coverage.covers: CNC-cut interlocking wood joints only. Gros: about 50 joints (51 entries in the English guide, as some appear twice) for solid wood frames and for board materials such as plywood, including knock-down (tool-free, detachable) furniture joints and joints with loose keys. WikiHouse: a complete building chassis made of CNC-cut plywood/OSB blocks joined with plywood bow-tie (TIE) connectors and slot-together parts; it is a system rather than a catalogue of joint types. IBOIS: generators for timber-plate joints (through tenons, chamfered tenons, finger joints, half-laps, dowels, tab-and-slot and dovetail plate joints) and 5-axis CNC and robot assembly
coverage.organisation: Gros: by what is joined and how they meet. Frame joints (Rahmen) split into lengthening (end-to-end), corner, cross and T-joints; board joints (Brett) split into lengthening, corner, slotting and T-joints; plus carcass/frame-structure joints (Gestell). Each joint has a letter code by shape (T = dovetail, P = jigsaw/puzzle, F = finger, K = cross, Z = tenon, G = gooseneck/ginkgo) [uncertain]. This works well for a beginner who knows what they are joining but not the names. WikiHouse: by building block (floor, wall, roof, lintel) and connection (bow ties). IBOIS compas_wood: by contact type between plates (7 families: side-to-side in-plane, side-to-side out-of-plane, top-to-side, cross, top-to-top, side-to-side rotated, boundary), each with numbered joint-type codes
coverage.scope_match: low to medium: clever interlocking and knock-down joints fit the 'clever connection types' idea and can be laser-cut or CNC-cut by makers, but this is CNC woodwork joinery, which the project ranks lower priority; the Gros list is the best source for the wanted short list of interlocking CNC joints
coverage.taxonomy_used: Gros: 3 top-level groups (frame joints, board joints, carcass joints), each split by joint position (lengthening, corner, cross, T, slotting). compas_wood: 7 contact-type families with code ranges (1-9 side-to-side in-plane, 10-19 out-of-plane, 20-29 top-to-side, 30-39 cross, 40-49 top-to-top, 50-59 rotated, 60-69 boundary). Manis: joint functions (dowels, tenons, chamfered tenons, 'sunrise', custom finger/slot, fingers, half-lap). Robeller: multiple tab-and-slot joints with one degree of freedom (1DOF), assembled along a single insertion direction
coverage.example_types: From Gros: Shouldered Dovetail; Double Dovetail; Symmetrical Double Dovetail (modelled on the Japanese Ryo-men-ari-tsugi); Double Jigsaw (puzzle-shaped splice); Plain Scarf with Dovetail Keys (butterfly/bow-tie key); Gooseneck Mortise and Tenon with Stub Tenons; Ginkgo Scarf; Halving with Elliptical Tenon; Jigsaw Cross Halving; Hooked Jigsaw Halving; Stop Lap with Jigsaw Key; Secret Fingertip Tenons; Hammer Tenons; Clip Tenons; Catch Tenon (detachable corner); Slotting Girder Joint (tool-free shelf joint); Hooked Slotting Joint; Lengthening with Meander Key; Detachable Lengthening with Key; Locked Leg Framing (removable); 3-Dimensional Finger Tenon; Tenon Joint with Star-Shaped Mortise. From WikiHouse: plywood bow-tie (TIE) connector. From IBOIS: multiple tab-and-slot plate joint (through tenon), chamfered tenon, dogbone and T-bone corner reliefs for CNC cutting
coverage.making_methods: CNC routing (3-axis for Gros and WikiHouse, 5-axis for IBOIS), laser cutting (Gros joints per the GitHub repo), robotic assembly (IBOIS); materials are solid wood, plywood, OSB, LVL and cross-laminated timber
coverage.item_count: Gros: 50 joints (51 entries in the guide; the zip holds about 826 entries: 102 DXF, 51 IGES, 51 DGN and others, plus 217 PDF pages). WikiHouse Skylark 150: a library of standard blocks (only 3 room spans in v1.0; count of blocks not verified) [uncertain]. IBOIS: 7 compas_wood joint families; Manis offers about 7 joint generators
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Hand-release / knock-down: yes, Gros's slotting joints, Catch Tenon, Detachable Lengthening with Key and Locked Leg Framing are explicitly detachable and tool-free. Self-locking: yes, via keys and hooked or jigsaw shapes, and Robeller's 1DOF joints lock all but one sliding direction. Compliant or snap: possibly Gros's Clip Tenons [uncertain]; IBOIS has separate research on CNC snap-fit joints for wood panels (not opened) [uncertain]. Torque-limiting, ratchet, detent, over-centre, print-in-place, gear trains, powered connectors and adhesives: not covered (Robeller's thesis started with a hybrid of integral joints plus adhesive bonding, but gives no adhesive types)
coverage.entry_structure: Gros: joint name, rendered drawing, a paragraph on history, use and strength, an 'example of application' (e.g. Simplizissimus Table, Meander Shelf), and a file code linking to CAD/CAM files in several formats plus a machining tutorial. WikiHouse: block page with model, cutting files and metadata; engineering pages give design values. IBOIS: Grasshopper components and Python API docs with example scripts, a 3D viewer and videos
coverage.audience_level: Gros: hobbyist to professional furniture maker with a CNC router. WikiHouse: self-builders, architects, structural engineers and fabricators. IBOIS: research / professional computational designers

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: Gros's joints have plain descriptive English names (Jigsaw Cross Halving, Hammer Tenons) and short explanations, and the poster gives an at-a-glance overview, but the data files are in dated formats; WikiHouse is well documented but aimed at building a house; IBOIS tools are low (Rhino/Grasshopper scripting)
usefulness.has_images: yes: Gros has rendered drawings of each joint and a one-page poster of all 50; WikiHouse has photos and diagrams; IBOIS has renders and research images
usefulness.has_animations: partly: Gros has none in the guide, but there is a demonstration video by Ayse Esin Durmaz on YouTube (linked from the C-Lab page, not opened) [uncertain]; IBOIS has Vimeo tutorials and a trailer for Manis and an embedded 3D viewer in compas_wood docs; WikiHouse has assembly videos [uncertain]
usefulness.gaps: No 3D-printing versions or tolerances for printers; Gros gives few numbers beyond the 8 mm router bit; no strengths for most joints; the files need conversion to modern formats (no STEP, STL or SVG); no selector by load or removability; WikiHouse and IBOIS are about buildings and large plates, not small maker parts; IBOIS tools need paid Rhino
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: medium: there are no per-joint web pages for Gros's joints (all inside one zip and one poster), so link to the winterdienst or Open Up! page. WikiHouse engineering pages have stable per-topic URLs (e.g. https://www.wikihouse.cc/engineering/bow-ties). compas_wood has per-example doc pages (e.g. https://petrasvestartas.github.io/compas_wood/examples/joinery_parameters/)
usefulness.reusable_data: structured: Gros's joint list and CAD files can be reused non-commercially with credit and share-alike (CC BY-NC-SA); a GitHub re-packaging of the cutting files exists. WikiHouse block library is on GitHub and Airtable under CC BY-SA 4.0. IBOIS code is MIT (freely reusable, including the joint-family code scheme)
usefulness.maintained: Gros: static archive (CD-ROM content from 1997; download still online September 2026; the flexiblestream.de mirror link on winterdienst now returns 403, but jochen-gros.de hosts the zip). WikiHouse: active (Skylark v1.0 released with a roadmap; Skylark 200 files 'in progress'). IBOIS: Manis last noted around 2021 [uncertain]; compas_wood actively maintained in 2026
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: Gros's grid: first ask 'what are you joining (frame, board or carcass)?' then 'how do they meet (end-to-end, corner, cross, T, slot)?' This is a ready-made flow-chart branch for joints. Give every joint an 'example of application' photo. Offer one printable poster of all joints. compas_wood's contact-type families (side-to-side, top-to-side, cross and so on) and 'insertion direction' idea are good plain-language filters. WikiHouse shows how to publish tested design values next to a joint
usefulness.design_rules_given: Gros: designed for an 8 mm router bit; cut 1 mm per pass on the FBZ training machine; slotting joints are cut 2 mm narrower than the board thickness with a 2 mm groove extension so they fit despite thickness variation. WikiHouse bow ties: shear area 1008 mm², shear stiffness 3 kN/mm, tensile area 1008 mm², tensile stiffness 1.5 kN/mm, contact area at failure about 767 mm², with a capacity spreadsheet; the Materials 2025 study measured TIE joints in 18 mm plywood at about 7.7 kN in tension and 8.2 kN in shear (best variants). IBOIS: tool-radius offsets and dogbone/T-bone notch generation
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: yes for IBOIS: Manis and compas_wood generate joint geometry, CNC toolpaths and robot paths from plate models (Grasshopper/Python). WikiHouse: fixed blocks now, with parametric block models on its roadmap. Gros: fixed drawings only
usefulness.file_formats: Gros: DXF (2D, R10), IGES, DGN, MCD, VLM, CAD and SIM (2 exchange, 3 native CAD and 2 CAM formats) plus PDF guide and PDF/PNG poster. WikiHouse: cutting files and 3D models in several formats, plus GitHub and Airtable data (exact formats not verified) [uncertain]. IBOIS: Grasshopper .gh/.ghpy, Python, G-code, robot trajectories, finite element models
usefulness.terminology_value: medium: Gros gives clear English and German names for CNC-adapted joints and links some to their Japanese originals; compas_wood gives a systematic contact-type vocabulary; WikiHouse terms (bow tie, TIE joint, block) are system-specific
usefulness.decision_support: Gros's frame/board/carcass and lengthening/corner/cross/T/slot grid acts as a simple two-step selector. WikiHouse gives rules of thumb (e.g. minimum lengths of solid bracing wall per 6 m) and a bow-tie capacity spreadsheet. IBOIS tools pick joints by contact type automatically. No comparison tables across joint types
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Gros's joints are CNC reinterpretations of traditional European and Japanese joints (e.g. Symmetrical Double Dovetail from Ryo-men-ari-tsugi), so they overlap with the Japanese joinery catalogues item; the ayseesindurmaz GitHub repo and the Meredith Scheff-King poster (Instructables, Make:) are derived from Gros. Robeller's IBOIS joints were inspired by cabinetmaking joints; Manis and compas_wood overlap with each other. Overlaps with the HCI fabrication joints item (Zheng's Joinery, kyub) and Boxes.py for laser-cut finger joints
